name: Custom Window Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Window Stickers for Storefronts, Offices and Cars
seoDescription: Custom window stickers on clear, white, frosted, perforated or static cling film. Inside or outside glass mounting, die cut shapes, free proof, US shipping.
tagline: Printed for glass: hours, logos, promotions and privacy film, mounted inside or outside the window.
quickAnswer: Custom window stickers are printed graphics made for glass, on clear vinyl, opaque white vinyl, frosted film, perforated one-way film or static cling. They can be mounted on the outside of the glass or reverse-printed to face out from inside. Storefronts, offices and vehicles use them for hours, logos and promotions. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Material: clear, white, frosted, perforated, cling
Finish: gloss or matte, laminated option

sections.h2: Glass is a different surface, so the sticker is built differently
sections.html:
A sticker on a shop window gets read from both sides, sits in direct sun for most of the day and has to come off cleanly when the sale ends. That is why we treat window stickers as their own product rather than a clear sticker stuck on glass. The nearest sibling, our custom clear sticker range, is a transparent material you can put on any smooth surface, from a bottle to a laptop. Window stickers add the glass-specific choices: reverse printing so the graphic faces out from inside the window, opaque white backing so the colors do not wash out against daylight, frosted film for privacy and perforated film that reads as a solid image outside while staff still see the street.

Typical jobs are store hours by the door, a logo in the corner of each pane, seasonal offers, "now hiring" panels, office partition lettering and dealer or club decals on car rear windows. Pick the mounting side and film first, then the size, then the shape.

sections.h2: Inside the glass or outside: pick the mounting before anything else
sections.html:
Mounting side decides which film you need. An inside-glass sticker is printed mirrored on the back of clear film, with the adhesive on the printed face, so it shows correctly through the window and the glass itself protects the ink from rain, car washes and vandals. An outside sticker is printed normally and gets a laminate instead. The table lists what we print and when each one makes sense.

If the glass is tinted or low-E coated, tell us. Tinted glass darkens an inside-mounted graphic, and some coatings do not like adhesive, so we may suggest an outside mount with laminate instead.

sections.h2: Sizes that fit a door, a pane or a rear window
sections.html:
Window stickers run bigger than most sticker jobs. We print from 0.5" up to 24" x 36" in a single piece, and larger storefront graphics are tiled as panels that butt together on the glass.

  • Hours of business: 8" x 10" or 10" x 12" clear vinyl, reverse printed, mounted inside at eye level by the door handle.
  • Corner logo: 4" to 8" die cut to the logo outline, one per pane, so the branding repeats without blocking the display.
  • Sale or seasonal panel: 18" x 24" opaque white, outside mount, swapped every few weeks.
  • Full-window ad: perforated film tiled to the pane, usually 24" wide strips so one person can hang it.
  • Car rear window decal: 4" x 6" to 6" x 12" clear or white vinyl, outside mount with laminate.
  • Privacy band: frosted film, 24" tall by the width of the partition, with a logo knocked out of the frost.

Send the pane measurements with your artwork and we will set the panel splits so seams land in quiet areas of the design, not through a line of text.

sections.h2: Sun through glass is the hardest thing a sticker faces
sections.html:
South and west facing windows cook a sticker. The glass traps heat against the film, and UV comes straight through, so cheap paper window signs curl and fade within a season. Our window films are UV-stable vinyl, and on outside mounts we add a gloss or matte laminate that takes the weather instead of the ink. Inside mounts last longer still because the glass shields them. For graphics that live on exterior walls, doors and signs rather than on glass, the outdoor sticker page covers the heavier films rated for years in rain and sun.

Cleaning is the other wear point. Ammonia-based glass cleaners dull an unlaminated print over time, so a laminated outside mount or an inside mount is the right call for anything that has to survive a weekly window wash.

sections.h2: How to order custom window stickers
sections.html:
1. Measure the glass and note which side you will mount from. Mark any tint, frosting or mullions in a quick photo.
  2. Choose the film from the table above: clear for logos and hours, white for promotions, frosted for privacy, perforated for full-window ads, cling for short runs.
  3. Send artwork as vector (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size. For inside mounts we mirror the file for you.
  4. Tell us the quantity. The minimum is 100 stickers, which for a chain of stores or a club decal run is usually the right number anyway.
  5. Approve the free digital proof. We show the cut line, the mount side and the reading direction so there are no surprises on the glass.
  6. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after approval, with free FedEx shipping in the United States and delivery inside 8 to 10 business days.

Need the hours sticker for one location plus logo decals for six more? Mixed sizes can go on one order; pricing is set by size, quantity and film, starting at $0.30 per sticker, and the full product list sits on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

sections.h2: Applying a window sticker without bubbles or crooked edges
sections.html: Clean the glass with soap and water, not glass cleaner, and let it dry. For anything over about 12" use the wet method: mist the glass with water and a drop of dish soap, position the sticker, then squeegee from the center out and leave it overnight to set. Small decals go on dry with a hinge of masking tape along the top edge. Apply above 50°F; cold glass stops the adhesive from grabbing. When a promotion ends, warm the sticker with a hair dryer, peel from one corner at a low angle and the removable adhesive leaves the glass clean. Permanent adhesive is available for decals that should never be peeled by passers-by, such as safety or regulatory marks.

faqs.q: Can custom window stickers be printed to read correctly from inside the glass?
faqs.a: Yes. For an inside mount we mirror the artwork and print it on the back of clear vinyl, with the adhesive over the printed face. Stuck to the inside of the window, it reads the right way round from the street, and the glass protects the ink from weather and cleaning.

faqs.q: Will a window sticker block the view out of my storefront?
faqs.a: Only if you choose opaque white film. Clear vinyl shows just the printed art, frosted film lets light through while blurring the view, and perforated film prints a full image on the outside that staff can still see through from inside. Choose the film by how much view you want to keep.

faqs.q: Do window stickers come off glass cleanly when a promotion ends?
faqs.a: With our removable adhesive, yes. Warm the sticker for a few seconds with a hair dryer, lift a corner and peel slowly at a low angle. Any faint tack left behind wipes off with soapy water. Static cling has no adhesive at all and peels away in one piece.

faqs.q: How big can a single window sticker be for a storefront?
faqs.a: One piece can be up to 24" x 36". Anything larger, such as a full pane, is printed as panels that butt together on the glass. We plan the splits on the proof so seams fall in plain areas of the design rather than across text or faces.

faqs.q: Can I put custom window stickers on the outside of a car window?
faqs.a: Yes. Use clear or white vinyl with a laminate so it survives car washes and sun, and keep it to the rear or rear side windows; most states restrict stickers on the windshield and front side glass. Perforated film works on rear windows and still lets you see out.

faqs.q: What is the difference between static cling and adhesive window stickers?
faqs.a: Static cling is a soft vinyl that holds to glass by surface contact with no adhesive, so it peels off and resticks many times but only on smooth glass and only indoors or sheltered. Adhesive window stickers bond to the glass, survive weather and cleaning, and are the choice for anything staying up more than a month.

faqs.q: Can a logo be knocked out of a frosted privacy band?
faqs.a: Yes. We cut the logo or lettering out of the frosted film so clear glass shows through it, or print the logo in color on the frost. Both are common on office partitions and meeting-room glass where you want privacy at eye level without losing daylight.

faqs.q: How many window stickers do I have to order for one shop front?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers per design. For a single location that usually becomes a mix: a few large hours and logo pieces plus smaller decals for doors, cases and vehicles. Mixed sizes of the same artwork can share a run, so ask us to split the quantity.

faqs.q: Will sunlight through the glass fade a window sticker?
faqs.a: An unprotected print on a south-facing window fades within a season. Our window films are UV-stable vinyl, outside mounts get a laminate, and inside mounts sit behind the glass, which filters a good share of UV. Set up that way, a window sticker holds its color for years.

faqs.q: Can window stickers be die cut around a logo shape?
faqs.a: Yes. Die cut window decals follow the outline of the logo or lettering, with no background border, which is how most corner logos and dealer decals are done. For lettering with thin strokes we keep a thin clear border or a backing so the pieces apply as one unit.

faqs.q: Should a storefront window sticker be gloss or matte?
faqs.a: Matte reads better on glass that gets direct sun, because it kills the glare that makes gloss hard to read from the sidewalk at midday. Gloss gives deeper color and suits shaded windows and inside mounts, where the glass already provides a smooth glossy face.

faqs.q: How do I apply a large window sticker without bubbles?
faqs.a: Wash the glass with soap and water, mist it lightly with the same mix, position the sticker, then squeegee from the center outward to push the water to the edges. Leave it overnight before touching it. Apply above 50°F; on a cold pane the adhesive will not grab properly.
